title: Launch signal fabric and regional cohort scheduler for release trains (runtime/console/api)
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Problem: Coordinating release trains across runtime, console, and API surfaces is currently manual and error-prone. We need a lightweight orchestration layer ("signal fabric") that centralizes launch signals (capacity, quality, compliance, blackout windows) and computes cohorted schedules per region/team. This ticket scopes the PM work to design the scheduling policy, stakeholder surface, and contractor handoffs for an initial pilot across EU and US regions.
background: Current practice: PMs coordinate channels, spreadsheets, and ad-hoc Slack threads for launch windows. Engineering implements per-service canaries and capacity reservations, but there is no canonical single source of truth or machine-checkable signals. Prior artifacts: initial discovery doc (Confluence), cost simulation (Sheets), and the launch cadence audit from Q4 2025.
goals: Define an opinionated 'launch signal' model that captures capacity, quality, security, and blackout constraints
Design a regional cohort scheduler that generates per-team windows and conflict resolution rules
Create PM-owned UX surface in Console and an API contract for eng teams to consume launch signals
Pilot with runtime + console + API teams for two coordinated releases without manual escalation
success_metrics: Reduce manual scheduling sync meetings by 60% for coordinated launches within pilot teams
90% of launches in pilot use machine-generated windows from the scheduler
Zero high-severity launch conflicts due to missed blackout or capacity constraints during pilot
Mean time to recovery for rollout issues reduced by 25% due to clearer fallback lanes
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated signal model documented in Confluence and approved by Eng/Design/Security
Console mock for 'Launch scheduler' validated in design review and linked in ticket
Public API spec (OpenAPI) for launch signals created and a stub implemented by runtime team
Pilot runbook with roles, escalation, and checklist available and used for first two pilots
Cross-team retrospective with metrics captured and next-step recommendations
